 -4-  NC: 2024:KHC:37407  MFA No. 1013 of 2020  C/W MFA No. 1678 of 2020 CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE H.T. NARENDRA PRASAD  ORAL JUDGMENT 1. MFA No.1678/2020 is filed by the Insurance Company and MFA No.1013/2020 is filed by the claimants under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act',
The United India Insurance Company ... vs Smt. Pushpa on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5492315/
3 for short) challenging the judgment and award dated 13.09.2019 passed by the MACT, Udupi in MVC No.764/2017.
2.

Facts giving rise to the filing of the appeals briefly stated are that on 27.03.2017 at about 04.30 p.m., the deceased Sanjeeva Moolya was riding motorcycle bearing Registration No.KA-20-EH-3654 from Karkala side towards Udupi side in a slow and careful manner and at that time, the driver of the Maruthi Alto Car bearing Registration No.KA-51-N-9154 drove the same from Udupi towards Karkala side in a very rash and negligent manner, came to extreme wrong side of the road and dashed the NC: 2024:KHC:37407 motorcycle of the deceased.

As a result of the aforesaid accident,
the deceased sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries.
3. The claimants filed a petition under Section 166 of the Act seeking compensation for the death of the deceased along with interest.
4. Upon service of notice, the respondent Nos.1 and 2 appeared through counsel and respondent No.2 only filed written statement denying the averments made in the claim petition.

5. On the basis of the pleadings of the parties, the Claims Tribunal framed the issues and thereafter,
recorded the evidence.

The claimants, in order to prove the case, examined claimant No.1 as PW-1,
and other three witnesses as PW-2 to PW-4, and got exhibited documents namely Ex.P1 to Ex.P16.

On behalf of respondents, no witness was examined and got exhibited a document NC:
2024:KHC:37407 namely Ex.R1.

The Claims Tribunal, by the impugned judgment, inter alia, held that the accident took place on account of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver, as a result of which, the deceased sustained injuries and succumbed to the injuries.

The Tribunal further held that the claimants are entitled to a compensation of Rs.25,63,864/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. and directed the Insurance Company to deposit the compensation amount along with interest.
Being aggrieved, these appeals have been filed.

6. The learned counsel for the claimants has raised the following contentions:
a) Firstly, the claimants assert that the deceased was aged about 58 years at the time of the accident and had a monthly income of Rs.31,351/- as a Head Master working in the Government School.
b) Secondly, as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of NATIONAL INSURANCE CO. LTD. -v- PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS [AIR 2017 NC: 2024:KHC:37407 SC 5157], in cases, where the deceased was a Government Employee, an addition of 15% of the established income towards 'future prospects' is warranted when the deceased was aged between the age group of 50-60 years.

sentences.text: This principle shall be considered in the present case.
But the Tribunal has erred in adding 10% towards 'future prospects'.
c) Thirdly, as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE CO.

The United India Insurance Company ... vs Smt. Pushpa on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5492315/
4 LTD. -V- NANU RAM [2018 ACJ 2782], each of the claimants is entitled to compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of 'loss of love and affection and consortium'.
d) Lastly, considering the age and avocation of the deceased, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is inadequate and on the lower side.

sentences.text: With the above contentions, the learned counsel sought to allow the appeal.

On the other hand, the learned counsel for the Insurance Company has raised the following counter- contentions:
a) Firstly, the deceased was a Government employee at the time of the accident.
He was aged about 58 years and he was left with one year and two months of service.
Therefore, the Tribunal without applying the split multiplier method, has erred in adopting a multiplier as '9', which is contrary to the material available on record.
b) Secondly, on appreciation of oral and documentary evidence and considering the age and avocation of the deceased, the overall compensation awarded by the Tribunal is just and reasonable.

With the above contentions, the learned counsel sought to dismiss the appeal.
8.
Heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the judgment and award of the Tribunal.
It is not in dispute that Sanjeeva Moolya died in the road traffic accident occurred on 27.03.2017 due to rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle by its driver.
10. At the time of the accident, the deceased was working as Head Master in Government School and was earning a monthly salary of Rs.31,351/-.
The Tribunal after deducting professional tax, has rightly considered the annual income of the deceased at Rs,3,73,812/-.

The Apex Court in Civil Appeal No.6451 of 2021 (Arising out of S.L.P.(C)No.14558 of 2019 decided on 25.10.2021) has held that split multiplier cannot be applied while calculating the 'loss of dependency.
Therefore, the submission of the learned counsel appearing for the Insurance Company that application split multiplier in this case is untenable.

11. In view of the law laid down by the Constitution Bench of the Supreme Court in 'PRANAY SETHI'
(supra), to the aforesaid income, 15% has to be added on account - 10 - The United India Insurance Company ... vs Smt. Pushpa on 12 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5492315/
5 NC: 2024:KHC:37407 of future prospects.

entities.text: United India Insurance Company ... vs Smt. Pushpa
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the annual income comes to Rs.4,29,884/-.
The Tribunal has rightly taken 1/3rd of the income of the deceased towards personal expenses and remaining amount has to be taken as his contribution to the family.
The deceased was aged about 58 years at the time of the accident and multiplier applicable to his age group is '9'.

Thus, the claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.25,79,304/- (Rs.4,29,884*9*2/3) on account of 'loss of dependency'.
12.
In addition, the claimants are entitled to compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of 'loss of estate' and compensation of Rs.15,000/- on account of 'funeral expenses'.
Claimant No.1, wife of the deceased is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/- under the head of 'loss of spousal consortium'.

13. In view of the law laid down by the Supreme Court in the case of 'MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE' (supra), claimant Nos.2 and 3, children of the deceased are entitled - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:37407 for compensation of Rs.40,000/- each under the head of 'loss of parental consortium'.
14.

Thus, the claimants are entitled to the following compensation:
 Compensation under Amount in  different Heads (Rs.)
 Loss of dependency 25,79,304  Funeral expenses 15,000  Loss of estate 15,000  Loss of spousal consortium 40,000  Loss of Parental consortium 80,000  Total 27,29,304 15.

In the result, the following order is passed:
ORDER a) The appeal filed by the Insurance Company is dismissed.
The appeal filed by the claimants is allowed in part.
b) The judgment of the Claims Tribunal is modified.
